pencereler.0-5: Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart during re-entry. All seven astronauts were killed minutes before
pencereler.5-12: landing. The damage happened sixteen days earlier, at launch. A piece of insulating foam hit the left wing. It
pencereler.12-20: punched a hole in the heat shield panel. On re-entry, superheated gas poured into the wing. The structure melted from the inside.
pencereler.20-30: After that, every shuttle's heat shield was inspected in orbit.

segmentler.metin: Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart during re-entry.
It took only a suitcase-sized piece of foam hitting the left wing at launch.
So how could a suitcase-sized piece of foam hitting the left wing at launch do this?
The answer is foam strike breaching a reinforced carbon-carbon panel on the wing's leading edge — and it is why shuttles were inspected in orbit for heat-shield damage on every later flight.
